seo.title: HubGet vs Ninite – comparison
seo.description: HubGet vs Ninite: more than 25,000 apps with install, updates and uninstall right in the app, or around 150 hand-picked apps in one installer?
seo.ogDescription: An app store with 25,000+ apps, or an installer for around 150 hand-picked apps? A feature comparison of HubGet and Ninite.

texty.t5: Ninite showed that installing several apps at once doesn’t have to be a chore: check the apps, download one installer and you’re done. HubGet builds on that – with a catalog of more than 25,000 apps, an overview of everything on your PC, and updates and uninstalls right in the app.

texty.t107: Is HubGet a good alternative to Ninite?
texty.t108: Yes, especially if you want more than a one-off install. Like Ninite, HubGet installs without wizards or bundled extras – but it offers more than 25,000 apps, shows every app on your PC, keeps track of updates and can uninstall apps too.
texty.t109: Will I find the apps I know from Ninite in HubGet?
texty.t110: Common apps from Ninite, such as Chrome, Firefox, VLC, 7-Zip or Notepad++, are in the WinGet repository and therefore in the HubGet catalog. Save them to your own package bundle and next time install them all at once.
texty.t111: Is HubGet free for businesses too?
texty.t112: Yes. HubGet is open source under the MIT license and free to use at home and at work. An MSI installer is available for company-wide deployment.
texty.t113: Why does HubGet need to be installed when Ninite is just a download?
texty.t114: HubGet is a desktop app – that’s the only way it can show what’s installed on your PC, keep track of updates and let installs finish in the background. The installer is about 6 MB and doesn’t need admin rights.
